title: Power Plant — Fwd Engine Mount — Installation of Fire-Resistant Sleeving and Renewed Seals
abstract: On-wing installation of silicone-glass fire-resistant sleeving and a fluorosilicone seal set at the forward engine mount plane, bringing the drain and vent line protection back inside its qualification envelope.

sections.planning_reason: An instrumented thermal survey showed that the region immediately aft of the forward engine mount runs 40 to 55 degrees hotter in the cruise than the temperature used to qualify the sleeving fitted at build. No failure has occurred, but the sleeving is outside its qualification envelope and operators have reported hardened and cracked sleeving at engine change. This Service Bulletin restores the qualification margin without waiting for an in-service finding.
sections.description: The sleeving on the drain and vent lines that cross the forward mount plane is replaced by silicone-glass material qualified to the higher temperature and retained on the existing standoffs. The interface seal is replaced by a fluorosilicone item and the drain nozzle is replaced by a shorter, stiffer part so that the sleeve termination sits clear of the mount link. The mount itself is not de-loaded and the engine stays on the wing.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the fan cowl doors and make the engine safe for maintenance. Get access to the forward mount plane in zones 456 and 462. Do the inspection steps of task AMM-M-71-20-11-200-014-A on the existing sleeving and record its condition. Disconnect the drain and vent lines at the mount plane and cap the open ends. Remove the existing sleeving and clean the line surfaces. Install the seal D7120112839155 and the drain nozzle D7120115408026, then check the clearance to the mount link D7120111938052 against the figure in the accomplishment instructions. Fit the new sleeving and secure it at each standoff. Reconnect the lines and do a leak check at operating pressure. Close the fan cowl doors, do an engine ground run and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00327 that are still pre MOD-161477. The aircraft must already be at the steel side link fitting standard, because the sleeve termination clearance quoted in this Service Bulletin is measured to that fitting; aircraft still on the aluminium fitting need an individual clearance check.
sections.material_note: Kit K7120-1006-01 contains the sleeving for both engines, the seals, the drain nozzles and the retaining hardware. Lead time is eight weeks. The removed sleeving is not returnable. Two kits are needed if both engines are done at the same time; the kit is not split by engine position.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled fan cowl opening, or within 30 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
